_methodology: Cities selected based on meteorological research of 5 specific climate events that directly affect UP weather. Each city is an early indicator/source for a climate event that reaches UP with a documented lag time.

EVENT_1_LOO_HEATWAVE.description: Hot dry 'Loo' winds originate in the Thar Desert and travel west-to-east across the Indo-Gangetic Plain into UP. These cause severe heat waves in May-June.
EVENT_1_LOO_HEATWAVE.path: Thar Desert -> Eastern Rajasthan -> Haryana -> Delhi -> Western UP -> Eastern UP

EVENT_2_WESTERN_DISTURBANCE.description: Extratropical cyclonic storms from the Mediterranean that bring winter rain and cold waves to UP. They enter India from the northwest through J&K/HP.
EVENT_2_WESTERN_DISTURBANCE.path: J&K -> Himachal Pradesh -> Punjab/Haryana -> Delhi -> Western UP

EVENT_3_SW_MONSOON.description: Southwest Monsoon provides 85% of UP's annual rainfall. Two branches (Arabian Sea + Bay of Bengal) converge over the Gangetic plain. Onset Kerala June 1 -> UP by late June.
EVENT_3_SW_MONSOON.source_region: Kerala coast (onset) + Arabian Sea + Bay of Bengal
EVENT_3_SW_MONSOON.path_arabian: Kerala coast -> Western Ghats -> Central India (Narmada/Tapi valleys) -> Rajasthan -> UP
EVENT_3_SW_MONSOON.path_bengal: Bay of Bengal -> Odisha/WB coast -> Bihar -> Eastern UP
EVENT_3_SW_MONSOON.lead_time: 30-40 days from Kerala onset to full UP coverage
EVENT_3_SW_MONSOON.key_indicator: Monsoon trough normal position runs from NW Rajasthan through Prayagraj to Bay of Bengal

EVENT_4_BAY_DEPRESSION.description: Low pressure depressions/cyclones forming in the Bay of Bengal move west-northwest, bringing heavy rain to eastern UP. These are the primary cause of monsoon rainfall surges.
EVENT_4_BAY_DEPRESSION.path: Bay of Bengal -> Odisha/WB coast -> Jharkhand -> Bihar -> Eastern UP -> Central UP
EVENT_4_BAY_DEPRESSION.lead_time: 2-4 days from landfall to UP impact

EVENT_5_COLD_WAVE_FOG.description: Cold northwesterly winds combined with Western Disturbance moisture create dense fog blanket across the Indo-Gangetic Plain in winter (Dec-Feb). Affects agriculture and transport.
EVENT_5_COLD_WAVE_FOG.path: Punjab/Haryana -> Delhi -> Western UP -> Central UP -> Eastern UP
EVENT_5_COLD_WAVE_FOG.lead_time: 1-2 days, often moves NW to SE across IGP

cities.name: Bikaner
cities.role: Deep Thar desert — ground zero for Loo wind generation. Heat here = heat wave in UP in 2-3 days.

cities.name: Churu
cities.role: India's hottest recorded temperatures. Key heat wave origin point on the Loo wind corridor.

cities.name: Jaipur
cities.role: Eastern Rajasthan — Loo transit point. Heat here reaches western UP within 1-2 days.

cities.name: Hisar
cities.role: Haryana arid belt — last major station before Loo winds enter western UP. Also cold wave corridor.

cities.name: New Delhi
cities.role: Immediate UP neighbor. All 5 climate events pass through Delhi before reaching western UP. Universal early indicator.

cities.name: Srinagar
cities.role: First Indian city hit by WDs entering from Mediterranean. Snowfall here = cold wave in UP in 3-4 days.

cities.name: Shimla
cities.role: Key WD indicator in western Himalayas. Snow/rain here directly correlates with UP winter rainfall 2-3 days later.

cities.name: Amritsar
cities.role: Punjab plains — WD reaches here after crossing mountains. Rain here = UP rain in 1-2 days.

cities.name: Chandigarh
cities.role: Punjab-Haryana junction — WD and cold wave transit point between mountains and plains.

cities.name: Dehradun
cities.role: Himalayan foothills directly north of UP. WD precipitation here feeds Ganga-system rivers that affect UP flooding.

cities.name: Thiruvananthapuram
cities.role: Monsoon onset station. IMD declares monsoon onset based on 14 Kerala stations. Onset here = UP monsoon in 30-40 days.

cities.name: Mumbai
cities.role: Arabian Sea branch monsoon milestone. Mumbai arrival = monsoon reaches UP in ~15-20 days.

cities.name: Nagpur
cities.role: Geographic center of India. Monsoon trough position over Nagpur indicates active rainfall phase for central UP.

cities.name: Bhopal
cities.role: Central India — monsoon trough indicator. Heavy rain here precedes UP monsoon surge by 5-7 days.

cities.name: Gwalior
cities.role: Direct south neighbor of UP (Bundelkhand border). Last stop on Arabian Sea monsoon branch before entering UP.

cities.name: Bhubaneswar
cities.role: Cyclone/depression landfall zone. Bay depressions hit Odisha coast first, then move NW into UP in 2-4 days.

cities.name: Kolkata
cities.role: Bay of Bengal coast — cyclone/depression tracking station. Bay of Bengal branch monsoon enters India here.

cities.name: Ranchi
cities.role: Chota Nagpur plateau — Bay depressions cross Jharkhand before reaching eastern UP. Transit indicator.

cities.name: Patna
cities.role: Immediate east neighbor on Ganga plain. Same river system, shared flood dynamics. Bay moisture reaches here before eastern UP.
